and even his entry into parinirvāṇa— as well as the roots of goodness produced by seeing, hearing, or drawing near to him, and all such matters.
Furthermore, he addressed the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, speaking in verse and reiterating the preceding teaching.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra said to the Bodhisattva Nature-Arising Wondrous Virtue (Śrīgarbha): "O Son of the Buddha, this place is inconceivable;
it is through immeasurable dharmas that the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, has appeared. Why is this? It is not by means of a single condition, nor by a single..."
This matter is accomplished through the appearance of the Tathāgata. It is accomplished by means of ten immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of *asaṃkhyeya* matters.

That is to say, having heard and received the great rain-clouds of the Dharma from past Buddhas, one is able to arise from this, like the four kinds of great wisdom-wind-circles. The first is the *dhāraṇī* of mindfulness and retention without forgetting.

The wind-circle of wisdom that can sustain the great rain-clouds of the Tathāgata’s sublime Dharma; second, the wind-circle of great wisdom that gives birth to śamatha and vipaśyanā, which can exhaust all afflictions;
third, the wind-circle of great wisdom of skillful dedication, which can bring all roots of goodness to fulfillment;
fourth, the wind-circle of great wisdom that gives birth to the various adornments free from defilement.
The wheel causes all sentient beings who were transformed in the past to purify their roots of goodness, because they have accomplished the power of the Tathāgata’s untainted roots of goodness.
Thus the Tathāgata attains equal and perfect enlightenment; such is the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), which is without arising and without action.
And thus it is accomplished. O Son of the Buddha, this is the first sign of the appearance of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
This single sign is briefly indicated as an illustration for the ten subsequent signs of appearance. Furthermore, thirty-seven verses are used to recount the merits therein.
The Bodhisattva Samantabhadra addressed the bodhisattvas, saying: "The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha possesses..."
There are ten kinds of immeasurable bodies; furthermore, there are ten kinds of immeasurable sounds; furthermore, there are ten kinds of immeasurable minds;
furthermore, there are ten kinds of immeasurable practices to be performed; furthermore, there are ten kinds of immeasurable attainments of perfect enlightenment;
furthermore, there are ten kinds of immeasurable entries into nirvana; furthermore, there are ten kinds of immeasurable approaches. These constitute the eighty [immeasurables] above.
They planted roots of merit through the practice of vows for the appearance of the Tathāgata and immeasurable Dharma-gates.
When this Dharma was being taught, ten unspeakably many hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of worlds in each of the ten directions shook in six ways;
even throughout all worlds in the ten directions, it was likewise so. At that time, in each of the ten directions, beyond eighty unspeakably many...

Beyond as many worlds as there are atoms in hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of Buddha-fields, there appeared before him Tathāgatas equal in number to the atoms in eighty unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of Buddha-fields, all named Samantabhadra.
They spoke these words: "Excellent, Son of the Buddha! You are indeed able, through the majestic power of the Buddhas, to accord with the nature of phenomena."

He expounded the inconceivable dharma of the Tathāgata’s appearance. While this dharma was being taught, within this assembly, bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in a hundred thousand buddha-fields attained the samādhi of all bodhisattva supernormal powers and received the Buddha’s prophecy.
In one lifetime, they shall attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. Sentient beings as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field will all resolve their minds upon *bodhi*.
The vast practices and vows, as well as the vast majestic powers [of this stage], are fully contained within the sūtra itself in the "Chapter on the Appearance of the Tathāgata.
This "Chapter on the Appearance of the Tathāgata" constitutes the fruit of equality.

There are eight assemblies. Regarding the "Chapter on Leaving the World" (*Lokottara-parivarta*) spoken in the Hall of Universal Radiance (*Samantaprabhā-koṭṭa*) within the Bodhimanda during the third assembly:

it represents the Tathāgata, the World-Honored One, residing in the Hall of Universal Radiance at the Bodhimanda in the kingdom of Magadha, seated upon the Lotus-Treasury Lion Throne, together with an unspeakable number of hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of Buddha-fields as numerous as atoms of dust.
Accompanied by all these bodhisattvas—who shall attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* in a single lifetime—they had gathered from various lands in other directions.
Their names were Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, Samantanetra Bodhisattva, and so forth;
these ten "Universal" (*Samanta*) Bodhisattvas, and others like them, from ten unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of *nayuta* Buddha-fields.
Bodhisattvas as numerous as atoms all fully accomplished the practices and vows of Samantabhadra.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra entered a vast samādhi called "Adorned with Buddha-Flowers.

When he entered this samādhi, all worlds throughout the ten directions shook in six ways and eighteen manners, and a great sound resounded so that it was heard by everyone without exception. He then arose from the samādhi.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, knowing that the assembly had gathered, addressed the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, saying:
"O Son of the Buddha, what is the reliance of a bodhisattva? What is the extraordinary perception? What is the practice? What is the spiritual friend?
What is diligent vigor? How does the mind attain peace and stability? What is the maturing of sentient beings? And what is the precept?"
What is self-knowing of the prophecy? What is entering the bodhisattva stages? What is entering the state of a Tathāgata? What is entering the mental activities of sentient beings?
What is entering the worlds? What is entering the duration of eons? What is the teaching on the three periods of time? What is knowing the three periods of time?
What is sitting at the site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*)? And so forth, what is the turning [of the wheel of Dharma]?
The Wheel of Dharma. For what reason does the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, manifest parinirvāṇa? Excellent, Son of the Buddha! I pray that you will explain this to me.
Altogether there are two hundred dharma-gates of questions; within the single category of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, they are answered in ten ways, totaling two thousand dharma-gates of answers.
If one can receive and uphold them, it should be known that such a person will swiftly [attain realization].

He attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. When this chapter was being taught, immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable worlds in the ten directions all shook violently, and a great light shone everywhere.

The Buddhas of the ten directions all appeared before Samantabhadra Bodhisattva and praised him, saying: "Excellent, excellent! O son of good family, you are truly able to teach these bodhisattvas..."
The Flower of the Definitive Meaning of the Sphere of Practice and Merit of the Great Bodhisattvas;

the Chapter on the Dharma Gate of Universal Entry into All Buddha-Dharmas and World-Transcending Dharmas. We Buddhas, all with one mind, shall protect and uphold this sutra, so that all bodhisattvas of the present and future who have not yet heard it may all hear it. At that time, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra...
The Bodhisattva, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the entire great assembly throughout the ten directions and as far as the dharma-realm, and spoke in verse.
Furthermore, he restated the merits of this chapter with two hundred stanzas, as fully contained within the sutra itself.
This "Chapter on Leaving the World" constitutes the section on practice, encompassing both the causes and effects of the accomplishment of conduct.
The Ninth Assembly in the Jeta Grove: Regarding the "Entry into the Dharma Realm" Chapter, it signifies that the World-Honored One was in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park, at Śrāvastī,
within a great and magnificently adorned multi-storied pavilion, together with five hundred bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
with Samantabhadra and Mañjuśrī as their leaders, and the bodhisattvas Jvālāketu and Dharmadhātuprabhāsa.

...and so forth. Because they have all fully accomplished the sphere of Samantabhadra’s practices and vows, he was accompanied by five hundred śrāvakas as well as immeasurable lords of the world, all of whom had previously made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas.
At that time, the bodhisattvas, the great virtuous śrāvakas, the worldly kings, and their retinues all thought to themselves: "What is this?"
The realm of the Tathāgata, the wisdom and conduct of the Tathāgata, the empowerment of the Tathāgata, the powers of the Tathāgata, the fearlessnesses of the Tathāgata, the samādhis of the Tathāgata,
the masteries of the Tathāgata, the body of the Tathāgata, and the wisdom of the Tathāgata— none of the gods or humans in all the worlds are able to penetrate them,
none are able to enter them, none are able to proclaim and clarify them, and none have the power to cause sentient beings to understand them.

[It is] understood. Except for the power of the Tathāgata’s empowerment, we pray that the World-Honored One, in accordance with the various inclinations, various liberations, various wisdoms, and even the various ways of hearing and receiving the teachings spoken by us and all sentient beings, will reveal the Tathāgata’s past aspiration for the mind of omniscience and such dharmas as these. We pray—

He explained it for them all. At that time, the World-Honored One, knowing the thoughts in the minds of the bodhisattvas, took great compassion as his body, great compassion as his gateway, and employed skillful means to fill the entirety of empty space. Then, the World-Honored One entered the Lion’s Stretching Samādhi.
Having entered this samādhi, the entire world was universally adorned and purified; at that moment, this Great Adornment—
The multi-storied pavilion suddenly became vast and expansive, without limit.
Boundless realms all emitted radiance, pervading the entire Dharma-realm, equal in measure to as many Buddha-fields as there are atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-lands.
Unspeakable jewels were spread across its ground. At that time, within the void above the Jeta Grove, there appeared an inconceivable...
Clouds of celestial palaces, music, songs of praise, and all manner of ritual offerings filled the void and pervaded the entire Dharma-realm.

At that time, from beyond worlds as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields in each of the ten directions, there came to the presence of the Buddha, from each of those ten directions, bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields. As...
Each of these bodhisattvas led an incalculable number of bodhisattvas, as numerous as the atoms in an unspeakable number of buddha-fields, to the presence of the Buddha.
Each manifested all manner of offering articles and ornaments, making offerings to the World-Honored One that pervaded the entire dharma-realm and filled the void of space.
According to the direction from which they came, each transformed themselves into jeweled lotus lion-thrones.

Seated with their retinues, they sat in the full lotus posture. In this manner, all the bodhisattvas of the ten directions, together with their retinues, were born from the conduct and vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
With the eye of pure wisdom, they beheld the Buddhas of the three periods of time;
having universally heard the ocean of sūtras of the wheel of Dharma turned by all the Tathāgatas, they attained [the state of] all...
The Bodhisattvas reached the other shore of mastery. Thus, the Bodhisattvas filled the Jeta Grove; this was entirely through the majestic spiritual power of the Tathāgata.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vairocanapraṇidhānābhāsa and others—the ten-headed Bodhisattvas—each offered ten verses to praise the Tathāgata’s meritorious conduct and vows.
Together there were one hundred verses, which again recounted the Tathāgata’s qualities.

Within this Jeta Grove, amidst these vast and great miraculous manifestations, the World-Honored One, wishing to cause all bodhisattvas to dwell securely in the Tathāgata’s Great Lion-Stretch Samādhi, emitted a great radiance from the white tuft of hair between his eyebrows.
This light was named "The Door of Universally Illuminating the Dharma Realm of the Three Times. It [shone] with as many atoms as there are in unspeakably many Buddha-fields.
With these rays of light as their retinue, they universally illumined all the oceans of worlds and Buddha-lands throughout the ten directions.
At that time, the great assembly of bodhisattvas in the Jeta Grove saw everything:

within every single atom of all Buddha-fields throughout the entire dharma-realm and space-realm, there were Buddha-lands as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-fields, each appearing in its own kind.
The names of the various types, their various colors, and their various purities;

the dwellings and their forms—within all of these, there were great bodhisattvas seated upon lion thrones at sites of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*), having attained perfect awakening (*samyaksaṃbodhi*).
At that time, Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra each recounted, with ten verses, the various miraculous transformations that had occurred within the Jeta Grove. At that time, Mañjuśrī...
The Bodhisattva Suśīla emerged from his pavilion, accompanied by immeasurable fellow-practicing bodhisattvas, as well as the various devas, kings, and the eight classes of beings.

Departing from their respective abodes, they came to where the Buddha was. They circumambulated the World-Honored One to the right for immeasurable times and made offerings with all manner of ritual implements.
Having completed these offerings, they took their leave and traveled south toward the human realm.
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra and six thousand bhikṣus, together with various bodhisattvas,
traveled south in succession through the human realm until they reached the east of the City of Blessings (Puṇyavatī), where they stayed at a great stūpa within the Adorned Śāla Grove.
At that time, Mañjuśrī, together with his retinue, having arrived at this place, immediately preached the *Sūtra of the Universal Illumination of the Dharma Realm* right there,
with one hundred trillion nayutas of sūtras as its retinue. While he was preaching this sūtra,
immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of dragon kings and others within the great ocean heard it.

The teaching was concluded. Having developed a profound weariness with the dragon realm and seeking the path of the Buddha, they all cast off their dragon bodies and were reborn among gods and humans.
Ten thousand dragons attained non-retrogression regarding *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Furthermore, immeasurable sentient beings were each tamed within the three vehicles. At that time, the people of the city of Puṇḍravardhana heard of Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta...
The World-Honored One was staying at the Great Stūpa in the Forest of Adorned Banners. A vast multitude emerged from the city and came to where he was.
At that time, there was an upāsaka named Mahāmati, who was accompanied by five hundred upāsakas.
They came to the place where Mañjuśrī was. Furthermore, there were five hundred upāsikās, headed by Mahāmati, who came to his presence together with their retinues.
Additionally, there were five hundred youths, headed by Sudhana, who came together with their retinues.
They came to where he was. Furthermore, five hundred young maidens, with Samantabhadra at their head, arrived at that place together with their retinues.
Each of them prostrated at the feet of the youth Mañjuśrī, circumambulated him three times to the right, and withdrew to sit on one side.
At that time, the youth Mañjuśrī, knowing that the people of Puṇḍravardhana had all assembled, [proceeded] accordingly...
His mind was joyful. Manifesting a body of sovereign power, he was about to preach the Dharma for him.
At that time, he further observed Sudhana to see by what causes and conditions he had received his name.

He knew that when this youth was first born, within his residence there spontaneously appeared a pavilion made of the seven treasures; beneath the pavilion were seven hidden treasuries, and upon its seat, of itself—
However, it split open, and five hundred precious vessels emerged. These vessels were filled with various objects and immeasurable treasures.
His parents, relatives, and skilled physiognomists together called this boy Sudhana (Good Wealth).
They knew that this youth had already made offerings to countless Buddhas of the past, had deeply planted roots of goodness, and possessed vast faith and understanding. Constantly...
Delighting in the close attendance of spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), purifying the bodhisattva path, and seeking omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), he became a vessel for the Buddha-dharma.
Mañjuśrī expounded various essential teachings for him, causing the youth Sudhana’s mind to open and his understanding to be resolved;
he gave rise to the bodhicitta and attained great eloquence (*pratibhāna*). Furthermore, with thirty-four verses, [Mañjuśrī] reiterated the preceding teachings. At that time—
Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva turned his gaze toward Sudhana and spoke these words:
"Since you have resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and further wish to attend upon spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), inquire about the conduct of a bodhisattva,
and cultivate the path of a bodhisattva— O son of good family, by attending upon and making offerings to spiritual friends, you shall be endowed with all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*)."
This is the primary causal condition; therefore, do not give rise to weariness or discouragement here. Sudhana said: "I only pray that the Noble One will explain extensively for me:
how should one study the conduct of a bodhisattva? How should one cultivate the path of a bodhisattva? And even:
how may the conduct of Samantabhadra be swiftly brought to full perfection? At that time, Mañjuśrī again praised Sudhana with ten verses.

Virtue. This causes the youth Sudhana to be diligent and courageous, to draw near to spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), to cultivate the path of the bodhisattva, and to study the conduct of the bodhisattva, as well as his meritorious deeds and vows. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī addressed Sudhana, saying:
"To the south of here, there is a land called Suprabha. In that land, there is a mountain named Sumerukūṭa."
"In that mountain range, there is a bhikṣu named Meghashri. You should go and ask him: 'How does one learn the conduct of a bodhisattva?
How does one cultivate the path of a bodhisattva? How does one swiftly attain the full perfection of the conduct of Samantabhadra?
The bhikṣu Meghashri will explain this to you. When the youth Sudhana heard these words, he was filled with joy and leaped for gladness; he bowed his head...
He prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, and gazed up at him with earnest devotion, weeping tears of sorrow.
Then, taking his leave, he traveled south toward Mount Sumeru in the land of Sukhāvatī to approach the foremost spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra) and inquire about the methods for practicing the Way.
In this manner, he approached each of the fifty-three great spiritual friends one by one and asked his questions as before, having first resolved upon [the Bodhi-mind].
The mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. How does one study the bodhisattva practices? How does one cultivate the bodhisattva path?
And so on, up to: how does one swiftly attain the full perfection of the conduct of Samantabhadra?

Thus, each of these fifty-three great spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*) individually presented their own meritorious deeds, vows, powers, the dharma-gates for realizing the Way, and their supernormal powers (*abhijñā*).
[The Master] spoke thus to the youth Sudhana. This is why the youth Sudhana personally approached each of the spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra) and attained the dharma-gates of the fifty-three stages.
Thus, the first spiritual friend, the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, presides over fundamental wisdom (mūla-jñāna).
From the heart of the fundamentally unmoving wisdom (acala-jñāna), he gives rise to the ten...
One plants the seed of faith; with firm confidence, one initiates the practice of the ten abodes, the ten practices, the ten transferences, and the ten stages.
These forty types of preparatory effort (*prayoga*) serve as the practice of advancement.

Furthermore, through the perfected effort and practice of the eleventh stage, the stage of Equal Enlightenment (*samyak-saṃbodhi*), these five layers serve as the causes for advancement. Regarding the subsequent fifty...
These are the stages of spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*). Each has a stage of realized enlightenment as its fruit.
From the bhikṣu Meghaśrī up to the girl Maitreya-caryā, these ten spiritual friends preside over the Dharma-gate of the Ten Abodes (*daśabhūmi*).

Furthermore, from the bhikṣu Sudarśana up to the wandering ascetic Parivrājaka, these ten spiritual friends preside over the Dharma-gate of the Ten Practices (*daśacaryā*). Furthermore, the merchant Vāsantika...
From the goddess Uṣanti up to the goddess Anikṣiptadhura-vihāriṇī, these ten spiritual friends preside over the Dharma-gate of the Ten Dedications (*daśa-pariṇāmanā*).
Furthermore, from the goddess Vāsantī up to the goddess Gopā, these ten spiritual friends preside over the Dharma-gate of the Ten Grounds (*daśa-bhūmi*).
Furthermore, from Lady Māyā up to the youth Guṇakara and the maiden Guṇavatī, these ten spiritual friends... [preside over the Dharma-gate of the Ten Perfections].
The ten great samādhis of the Knowledge Lords and the fifty spiritual friends mentioned above constitute the fruits of the realization of the Way;
these are termed the fifty layers of cause and the fifty layers of fruit. Taken together, they form one hundred.
From the fundamental Immovable Wisdom arise the ten kinds of faith, which are termed the ten layers of cause and fruit. Thus, they constitute the one hundred and ten cities.
Regarding cause and effect: at the end, the youth Sudhana again draws near to Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva;
all his meritorious practices are perfected, and he returns to the fundamental, immovable seed-wisdom (*bīja-jñāna*).

He then draws near to Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, whereby the merit of the ten thousand practices is likewise fully perfected, and he accomplishes the conduct of Samantabhadra. Finally, he draws near to Maitreya Bodhisattva, who presides over the perfection of his meritorious practices.
The fruit of attaining Buddhahood. These fifty-three kinds of dharma-gates are each personally realized; one primary [gate] leads to Buddhahood.

By means of these dharma-gates, they serve as models for the cultivation of merit and the progressive practice for realizing the fruit, enabling all great-minded beings in the world to cultivate the path.
